transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
President Trump says on social media that there's an energy ceasefire between Russia
and Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Zelensky says he supports the idea, but he still doesn't have the details
and Russia hasn't commented yet.
And here's Luke Garrett has more.
Every Sunday Zelensky said he wanted to deal with Russia that would bar the two warring
nations from attacking oil and diesel infrastructure.
Here he is on ABC News.
We are ready for a ceasefire.
We are ready to begin from any kind of steps of escalation.
We are ready for energy ceasefire, not to attack energy both sides.
Zelensky then committed to holding Ukrainian elections if there's a 60-day ceasefire with
Russia.
Later, Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, "effective immediately,"
but the deal has not been confirmed by Russia.
And Zelensky says he and NATO Secretary General Mark Ruta are still awaiting details on this
deal between Russia and Ukraine.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, the White House.
More than 100 people, including children, have died after a migrant boat capsized off
the coast of Djibouti.
That's according to the UN's migration agencies.
Officials say over 100 people are missing, as NPR's Jule Bright reports.
Officials say the boat was traveling from Djibouti to Yemen and was carrying at least 300 passengers.
More than 80 mostly Ethiopian migrants have been rescued.
The sea crossing between Djibouti and Yemen is a popular but dangerous route for migrants
from the Horn of Africa seeking to reach Gulf countries.
The UN's migration agency estimates that more than half a million people tried to move
along the route last year, and at least 900 people died or went missing along the way.
Jule Bright, NPR News, Vegas.
The remnants of Hurricane Isa-Esus are moving up the east coast, dumping heavy rain and
causing flooding, gusty winds, and the threat of tornadoes in places.
The National Weather Service has issued flood and tornado watches for part of the Mid-Atlantic.
Philippe Pappen is with the National Hurricane Center.
Rainfall is the primary hazard at this point.
The actual wind circulation associated with the storm has continued to spin down over
the higher terrain of the Appalachian Mountains.
But they are expecting, again, some isolated flooding threat here across the Appalachians.
And he says people need to watch out for water-logged trees that may topple over.
The storm hit Destin, Florida Friday night as a Category 2 storm and at least four deaths
are blamed on it.
Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is churning in the Pacific, and it's expected to make landfall
in Mexico today.
The Category 4 storm has maximum sustained winds of 145 miles an hour.
Forecasters say Simon could bring 10 to 20 inches of rain over parts of southwestern
Mexico.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Pope Leo says he's undergoing surgery to remove a nodule from his lung.
The 71-year-old says it's in the initial phase and it's localized and that the surgery
will take place in the next couple of days.
He's expected to stay in the hospital for about a week.
Leo made the announcement during a Sunday blessing and thanked the crowd for their support and
their prayers.
It's still not clear, though, if he intends to take a scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina
and Peru that was scheduled to take place early next month.
Pakistan has imposed emergency rule in the province run by the political party of imprisoned
Prime Minister Imran Khan.
As Betsy Joles reports from Islamabad, this comes a week after Khan's party began a
long march toward the capital.
The move effectively suspends the provincial government controlled by Khan's party,
Pakistan, Tariq and Saaf.
It hands some of those powers over to the federal government, which is run by two dynastic
political rivals of PTI and heavily influenced by the military.
It risks igniting significant political unrest.
The decision comes after talks between PTI and the federal government failed to halt
the march that has seen Khan supporters demanding his release.
The government says PTI's indifference about fighting terrorism in this border region with
Afghanistan justifies emergency rule.
For NPR News, I'm Betsy Joles in Islamabad.
Egypt says a restored version of a second century painting from the famous Fayyum Portraits
will travel abroad for the first time it'll be in Rome starting next month.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
